transcript.content: Hello, welcome in. What brings you to see me today?

Well, occupational health actually sent me. They're saying my weight is dangerously low... especially for someone running presses and doing fabrication work all day. But to be honest with you, I just thought I was getting leaner and more disciplined.
How do you feel about the possibility of gaining weight?

Honestly, it scares me. If I see the scale go up even a little bit, I... well, I panic. I just worry that I'm going to lose all the control I've worked so hard for, and then I'll just end up heavy again. I really don't want that to happen.
If you have menstrual cycles, have you noticed any changes, such as periods becoming irregular or stopping altogether?
I haven't really noticed any changes with that. Everything seems pretty normal to me, or at least nothing has stopped or gotten irregular that I've noticed.
Are you currently taking any birth control pills or other hormonal contraceptives?
No, I'm not taking any birth control pills or anything like that. Just... haven't needed to.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient presents with dangerously low body weight and an intense fear of weight gain, viewing extreme restriction as discipline. However, she denies amenorrhea and maintains normal menstrual function without hormonal contraception, failing to meet the full endocrine criteria for typical anorexia nervosa (F50.0), thereby meeting criteria for atypical anorexia nervosa (F50.1).
